exchange of young professionals, promotion and collaboration on transportation technologies,
mobility systems and infrastructure in identified areas.
In a joint press meet after the talks, Prime Minister Modi said, during their talks the
two sides identified new avenues for defence cooperation and deepened collaboration in nuclear
energy.

The discussions between Prime Minister Modi and the Swiss President were very wide-ranging.
They reviewed the entire spectrum of India-Switzerland relations and discussed ways to further deepen
bilateral cooperation in several areas, including trade and investment, innovation and AI, military
exchange and defence production, and nuclear energy.
Both sides also reaffirmed their commitment to peace, diplomacy and reform of global institutions.
The two leaders discussed the ongoing conflict situation in the world.
India's position is very clear regarding the Ukraine situation that New Delhi stands for
a diplomatic solution.
India also appreciated the role being played by Switzerland in finding a diplomatic solution
to the matter.
The Swiss President was highly appreciative of Prime Minister Modi's position, particularly
his message that it is not an era of war, but an era of peace.

External Affairs Minister Dr. Aishwarya Shankar has said, India's approach of multi-alignment
enables it to engage with all important players in the world, including U.S., Russia and China.
Dr. Aishwarya Shankar was addressing the fifth quarterly economic conclave in New
Delhi today on the theme, India and the World Adaptive by Design.
He opined that the world is moving towards multi-polarity, whose architecture and
geometry are very different from the way it used to be.
In a way what we would today call multi-alignment, which is we have partners who each have their
interests, each of these relationships is different, they have different challenges,
they have different opportunities. There was a time when you issue unique to India.
I think more and more countries today face that, which is how do you engage all the
important players in the world at the same time. At this time, where the U.S. is concerned,
it is one of our principal strategic partners. It is the largest economic account. It's
our biggest trade account. It's a very major critical defense partner."
Union ports, shipping and waterways minister Sarbanan Sonuwal today flagged off the
first international cargo vessel since independence, carrying methanol from Assam's Debrugar
to Bangladesh. The move marks the revival of the Brahmaputra as an international trade
route after nearly eight decades and is expected to provide the northeast with a direct, greener
and more cost-effective trade corridor, more from our Guwahati correspondent.

The new waterway link is expected to substantially reduce logistic costs for industries in

Four new airports will be developed in West Bengal over the next two years to strengthen
air connectivity in the state.
A memorandum of understanding to this effect was signed today between the centre and the
West Bengal government at Nauberna in the presence of Civil Aviation Minister K. Ramohan
Aitu and Chief Minister Shubhendra Adhikari.
Speaking at an event, the Civil Aviation Minister said, airports would be developed
at Charra in Puralia, Kalai Kunda in Pashtim-e-Tnipur, Balurghat in Dokshin-Dinajpur, and Haseemara
in Alipur-Dwar.
Haseemara and Kalai Kunda are particularly important with plans to establish civil enclaves
at both locations.
Kalai Kunda already has 2,700-metre runway capable of accommodating narrow-body aircraft
such as the Boeing 737 and Airbus A320, which could significantly enhance air connectivity
in the region.
Similarly, at Belur Ghat, the existing airship will be expanded to facilitate the commencement
of commercial air operations.
The M.U. also envisages the development of a new airport at Purnia.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of Jan Seva Sevdesh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues.
Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasen, the government has been ceaselessly working
towards achieving the goal of a Vixit Bharat by 2047.
Through inclusive development and social empowerment,
this dedication is transforming lives.
Today, in our special series,
we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action
through the introduction of Vande Bharat trains.
As India advances towards its vision of becoming a developed nation by 2047,
mobility has emerged as a central pillar of nation's development.
Vande Bharat Express stands out as the prominent initiative of the Indian Railways providing
faster, safer, more reliable, and passenger-centric rail travel across the country.
Launched in February 2019, the Vande Bharat Express commenced its service on the New Delhi
Varanasi route, launching the four new Vande Bharat Express trains from Varanasi in November
last year, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the trains like Vande Bharat
is laying the foundation for the next generation of Indian railways.
Talking to Akash Mani News, Gaurang Sukla of Uttar Pradesh has appreciated the service
of Vande Bharat train saying that it reflects the vision of Atmanir Bharat.
It is a symbol of India's rapidly transforming railway network.
It is bringing the major cities closer.
And what truly stand out is our experience of a passenger, which includes the comfortable
seating, its modern interior, automatic doors, bio vacuum toilets and more is the
safety.
India's first indigenously designed and manufactured semi-high-speed train Vande Bharat Express has
been developed to strengthen intercity rail services by combining modern technology, improved
passenger comfort and reduced journey times.
The train is fully air-conditioned, which has been designed for a maximum speed of up
to 180 km per hour.
More than 161-day-varice trains are operational nationwide, enhancing connectivity across major
corridors.
Anand Kumar, Akashwani News, Delhi.
The election commission of India has rejected the allegations of leader of the opposition
in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, that the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanish Kumar
has changed Form 6 of Special Intensive Revision, SIR, illegally and unilaterally.
The commission clarified that the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR
has been upheld by the Supreme Court. In a social media post, the commission also said
that the order related to SIR in Bihar was issued with the unanimous approval of the commission
on the 24th of June last year. The poll body also highlighted that the order has also been
upheld by the Supreme Court in its judgement, dated 27th of May this year. Earlier, the apex
court clarified that it has not approved any changes to Form 6 being used by the Election
Commission during SIR of electoral rolls. The government has refuted claims circulating
on social media that the Election Commission of India has taken down the press release
published on the 26th of last month. The fact-check unit of the Press Information Bureau has said
that the press release is available and has not been taken down by the commission.
The stage is set for by-elections to five assembly constituencies in Tamil Nadu,
Uchheri and West Bengal along with one Lok Sabha constituency in Assam.
Polling for all six seats will be held tomorrow, while counting of votes will
take place on Friday. The assembly seats going to polls are Maduran Takam and
Dharapuram in Tamil Nadu, Tattana Chawadi in Puducherry, and Reji Naga Rannandikram
in West Bengal. In a Sam, voting will be held for the Nagam Lok Sabha constituency.
President Draupadi Murmur has appointed Chief Justice of three High Courts as judges of
the Supreme Court of India. In a social media post, Law and Justice Minister Arjun Ram
Ekwal informed that the President appointed Chief Justice of Gujarat High Court Justice
Sunita Agarwal, Chief Justice of Delhi High Court Justice Devendra Kumar Padhyay
and Chief Justice of Telangana High Court, Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh as judges of the
Supreme Court.
American Scientist Karl Dysaroff and German Scientist Peter Hegemann and Hio Gnegel won
the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for developing a breakthrough technique
to decode the inner workings of the brain.
This method, known as optogenetics, acts as a light-sensitive switch, allowing scientists
to potentially map which cells are responsible for which function in the brain.
The Nobel Assembly of Sweden's Karolinska Institute made the announcement today.
The Nobel committee said in a statement that the German duo of Hegemann and Negell discovered
a protein in algae known as channel rodopsin before American scientists Deiseroth transformed
the protein into a light-controlled switch for nerve cells.
It added that the work has laid the foundation for a new era in neuroscience.
